subject: Telemetry logs, onshore fallback, and CCPA/CPRA service provider clarification
messages:
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey@brightleaf.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Brightleaf Legal <legal@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry logs & CCPA role clarification

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look at Brightleaf's questions. We're doing a quick compliance pass ahead of pilot kickoff and have two items where we need confirmation from Redwood:

1) Role under CCPA/CPRA: will Redwood sign as a "Service Provider" (limited-use) or are there circumstances we should expect Redwood to be treated as a "Processor/Operator" for any US-state privacy addendum language?

2) Telemetry & exports: we need detail on what telemetry is retained (query text, model responses, request metadata), default retention windows, and whether Redwood exports any logs or aggregates to third parties (subprocessors). Also: do you offer an onshore fallback (US-only hosting + no offshore subprocessors) for California residents? If so, what is the timeline and proof you can provide (SOC2, subprocessor list, export logs)?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the questions mapped to our contract exhibit (Brightleaf_DPA_Questions.xlsx).

Appreciate a short write-up we can circulate to legal.

Best,
Lindsey
Lindsey Park
Head of Platform Security, Brightleaf Analytics
From: irene_choi@redwood.com <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Lindsey Park <lindsey@brightleaf.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry logs & CCPA role clarification

Hi Lindsey — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a couple of follow-ups: 

- Role: For our hosted API product used in the pilot, Redwood operates as a "Service Provider" under CCPA/CPRA limited-use language (we do not resell or use customer data to train models). We can add language in the DPA addendum making that explicit and cross-referencing the US-state privacy exhibit.

- Telemetry retained: we separate operational telemetry (metrics/traces, IP/region, latency) from content telemetry (prompt text, responses). Default retention windows: operational telemetry 90 days by default; content-level request logs (prompt + response) 30 days and only retained for troubleshooting unless the customer opts-in for longer retention for analytics. We redact user identifiers for analytics exports by default.

- Subprocessors & exports: we maintain a dynamic subprocessor list (will share), and we do export telemetry to our monitoring partner for aggregate metrics only — no raw prompt/response exports unless explicitly enabled by the customer. For onshore fallback, we offer a US-only deployment option (Dedicated or Private) where subprocessors handling telemetry are onshore; that option requires a 6–8 week provisioning window for Dedicated capacity and a DPA amendment.

I'm attaching an annotated snippet of the DPA with suggested language (redwood-sp-annotated-clause.docx) that mirrors our standard SP/limited-use commitments.

Two asks for you/your legal team:
- Confirm whether Brightleaf requires absolute operator-binding language (i.e., contract language that prevents any model-training use even as an anonymized signal) or if limited-use with an explicit no-training clause suffices.
- If you need onshore-only subprocessors, confirm whether 6–8 weeks is workable and whether Brightleaf requires HSM-backed key custody for any customer-managed encryption keys.

If useful, I can loop in our compliance lead and the person who manages onshore provisioning to outline the timeline.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Lindsey Park <lindsey@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry logs & CCPA role clarification (technical details)

Adding a few technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side: 

- Categories: we treat telemetry in three buckets: 1) control plane metrics (host/instance, GPU utilization, request counts); 2) debug traces (KV cache events, sequence ids, limited request metadata); 3) content traces (full prompt + model output). Only (3) contains actual customer content.

- Retention & access: control plane metrics are retained for 90 days, debug traces are retained for 14 days, content traces are retained for 30 days by default. Access to content traces is restricted to a small ops group via RBAC and we log all accesses (audit trail).

- Exports: we push aggregated control-plane metrics to our monitoring vendor (US-based). We do not push content traces to vendors. If Brightleaf requires no external exports at all, Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured so that no monitoring vendor receives telemetry (we can ship a local metrics stack).

- Onshore fallback: we can provision a US-only Dedicated pool that avoids offshore subprocessors, and we can certify the snapshot of the subprocessor list at provisioning time. HSM-backed customer key custody is available as an add-on but will add ~2–3 weeks to provisioning for integration and testing.

- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report, subprocessor list, and an export log sample (redacted) showing aggregate metrics exports.

Happy to work with legal on clause-level language for the DPA; suggest we produce a short appendix that Brightleaf can sign onto.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor, Senior Director, Runtime Reliability
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey@brightleaf.com>

Cc: Brightleaf Legal <legal@brightleaf.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-01T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry logs & CCPA role clarification

Thanks — that's helpful and lines up with what our security team expected. A few follow-ups from legal before we move to an addendum: 

- Please send the sample DPA appendix with the explicit "no training on customer content" covenant and the SP/limited-use wording you referenced.
- We need SOC2 evidence and the current subprocessor list for our procurement intake (can be redacted for contact details).
- On the onshore fallback: the 6–8 week window + HSM option looks reasonable. Can you confirm an earliest provisioning ETA if we sign the Dedicated commitment this week? We also want a simple statement that Brightleaf's California resident data will not leave US regions under the onshore configuration.

Attaching Brightleaf_Topline_Reqs.pdf for the legal checklist (top lines).

If you can get the sample DPA appendix and evidence by next Tuesday (2026-07-07), we should be able to move to internal approvals quickly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this pilot matters to our timeline.

Best,
Lindsey
